review_type: static source and documented Windows Firewall precedence; original script never executed

findings.finding: Default outbound Block does not override existing explicit Allow rules; these are left enabled.
DNS TCP/UDP 53 exceptions have no interface/program/service restriction; configured physical DNS servers can remain directly reachable.
SSTP server TCP443 exception applies to any program/service/interface, not exclusively VPN transport.
RemoteAccess Allow covers all destinations and all RemoteAccess interfaces, not a selected profile or whitelist.
EmergencyReset forces outbound Allow on all profiles and deletes recovery receipt; this is not scoped restoration.
Failure during re-Enable may restore pre-kill-switch defaults and delete saved state, dropping previously active protection.
Status counts rule presence only; does not certify enabled filters, foreign Allows, IPv6, routing or disconnect behavior.
Picks first connected SSTP; resolves server IPv4 only; does not follow server/profile changes. Persistent default Block itself does not need a polling loop to fail closed for unmatched traffic.
No verified atomic/locked protected backup, rule image drift checks, or native readback before claiming enabled/restored.

changes_in_candidate: Read-only legacy rule detector now recognizes SSTP Kill Switch group; existing admission gate rejects co-activation. No old rules deleted/adopted; no firewall writes run.
